claim: Batch operations (SendMessageBatch, DeleteMessageBatch, and ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch) cost the same as other Amazon SQS requests, so grouping messages into batches can reduce your costs.
question: Do Amazon SQS batch operations cost more than other requests?

values.display: cost the same as other Amazon SQS requests

evidence.quote: Batch operations (SendMessageBatch, DeleteMessageBatch, and ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch) all cost the same as other Amazon SQS requests. By grouping messages into batches, you can reduce your Amazon SQS costs.

claim: You can transfer data between Amazon SQS and Amazon EC2 or AWS Lambda free of charge within a single Region.
question: Is data transfer between Amazon SQS and EC2 or Lambda charged?

values.display: free of charge within a single region

evidence.quote: You can transfer data between Amazon SQS and Amazon EC2 or AWS Lambda free of charge within a single region.

claim: You can delete all messages in an Amazon SQS queue by using the PurgeQueue action.
question: Can I delete all messages in a message queue without deleting the queue itself?

evidence.quote: You can delete all messages in an Amazon SQS message queue using the PurgeQueue action.

claim: You are responsible for deleting the message, and the deletion request acknowledges that you are done processing the message.
question: Why are there separate ReceiveMessage and DeleteMessage operations?

evidence.quote: You're responsible for deleting the message and the deletion request acknowledges that you’re done processing the message.

claim: If you do not delete a message, Amazon SQS will deliver it again when it receives another receive request.
question: What happens to a received message that is not deleted?

evidence.quote: If you don’t delete the message, Amazon SQS will deliver it again when it receives another receive request.

claim: A deleted message is never received again from a FIFO queue. From a standard queue, under rare circumstances, you might receive a previously-deleted message a second time.
question: Can a deleted message be received again?

values.display: FIFO queues never introduce duplicate messages

evidence.quote: No. FIFO queues never introduce duplicate messages.
For standard queues, under rare circumstances, you might receive a previously-deleted message a second time.

claim: When you issue a DeleteMessage request on a previously-deleted message, Amazon SQS returns a success response.
question: What happens if I issue a DeleteMessage request on a previously-deleted message?

evidence.quote: When you issue a DeleteMessage request on a previously-deleted message, Amazon SQS returns a success response.

claim: Any duplicates that a message producer introduces into a FIFO queue are removed within a 5-minute deduplication interval.
question: How long is the deduplication interval of an Amazon SQS FIFO queue?

evidence.quote: Any duplicates introduced by the message producer are removed within a 5-minute deduplication interval.

claim: If you use a standard queue, you must design your applications to be idempotent, so processing the same message more than once does not affect them adversely.
question: What must an application do when it reads from an Amazon SQS standard queue?

values.display: design your applications to be idempotent

evidence.quote: If you use a standard queue, you must design your applications to be idempotent (that is, they must not be affected adversely when processing the same message more than once).

claim: By default, FIFO queues support up to 3,000 messages per second with batching, or up to 300 messages per second (300 send, receive, or delete operations per second) without batching.
question: What is the default throughput quota of an Amazon SQS FIFO queue?

evidence.quote: By default, FIFO queues support up to 3,000 messages per second with batching or up to 300 messages per second (300 send, receive, or delete operations per second) without batching.

claim: If you require higher throughput, you can enable high throughput mode for FIFO on the Amazon SQS console, which supports up to 70,000 messages per second without batching and even higher with batching.
question: How can I get higher throughput from an Amazon SQS FIFO queue?

qualifiers.scope: per FIFO queue, high throughput mode

evidence.quote: If you require higher throughput, you can enable high throughput mode for FIFO on the Amazon SQS console, which will support up to 70,000 messages per second without batching and even higher with batching.

note: The quotas page gives 70,000 TPS only for some Regions and lower values elsewhere; the FAQ gives no Region.

claim: The name of a FIFO queue must end with the .fifo suffix, and the suffix counts toward the 80-character queue name limit.
question: What must the name of an Amazon SQS FIFO queue end with?

evidence.quote: The name of a FIFO queue must end with the .fifo suffix. The suffix counts towards the 80-character queue name limits.

claim: For each message group ID, all messages are sent and received in strict order. Messages with different message group ID values might be sent and received out of order.
question: What are message groups in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue?

evidence.quote: For each message group ID, all messages are sent and received in strict order. However, messages with different message group ID values might be sent and received out of order.

claim: You must associate a message group ID with every message sent to a FIFO queue. If you do not provide a message group ID, the action fails.
question: Is a message group ID required when sending to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue?

values.display: must associate a message group ID

evidence.quote: You must associate a message group ID with a message. If you don't provide a message group ID, the action fails.

claim: By design, FIFO queues do not serve messages from the same message group to more than one consumer at a time. A FIFO queue with multiple message groups can serve different groups to different consumers in parallel.
question: Do Amazon SQS FIFO queues support multiple consumers?

values.display: more than one consumer at a time
different message groups to different consumers

evidence.quote: By design, Amazon SQS FIFO queues don't serve messages from the same message group to more than one consumer at a time. However, if your FIFO queue has multiple message groups, you can take advantage of parallel consumers, allowing Amazon SQS to serve messages from different message groups to different consumers.

claim: If multiple producers send messages in parallel without waiting for the success response of SendMessage or SendMessageBatch, the order between producers might not be preserved.
question: Do Amazon SQS FIFO queues support multiple producers?

values.display: order between producers might not be preserved
without waiting for the success response

evidence.quote: If multiple producers send messages in parallel, without waiting for the success response from SendMessage or SendMessageBatch actions, the order between producers might not be preserved.

claim: Some AWS or external services that send notifications to Amazon SQS might not be compatible with FIFO queues, even though they let you set a FIFO queue as a target.
question: With which AWS or external services are Amazon SQS FIFO queues compatible?

values.display: might not be compatible with FIFO queues
set a FIFO queue as a target

evidence.quote: Some AWS or external services that send notifications to Amazon SQS might not be compatible with FIFO queues, despite allowing you to set a FIFO queue as a target.

claim: FIFO queues support all metrics that standard queues support, and for FIFO queues all approximate metrics return accurate counts.
question: Which CloudWatch metrics do Amazon SQS FIFO queues support?

values.display: all metrics that standard queues support

evidence.quote: FIFO queues support all metrics that standard queues support. For FIFO queues, all approximate metrics return accurate counts.
